original_question: Suppose α is an endomorphism of a group G such that for every group H and every homomorphism f: G → H, there exists an endomorphism βf of H such that βf f = f α. Must α then be either an inner automorphism of G or the trivial endomorphism? This is Question 5 in(G. M. Bergman, Publ. Matem., 56(2012), 91–126).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.14 in arXiv:1401.0300 (The Kourovka Notebook, New Problems, 21st issue), which records Bergman’s group-theoretic open problem in the simplified equivalent form.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the Kourovka Notebook statement very closely: it quantifies over all groups H and all homomorphisms f: G → H, uses the commuting condition βf ∘ f = f ∘ α, and asks exactly the same dichotomy that appears in Problem 21.14, namely whether α must be an inner automorphism or the trivial endomorphism. It also correctly identifies the underlying source as Bergman’s Question 5.
missing_details: The original Bergman formulation is the equivalent functorial coherence question: whether the maps βf can be chosen coherently to define an endomorphism of the forgetful functor (G↓Group) → Group.
To be fully stand-alone, one should specify that G is arbitrary, H ranges over all groups, and f ranges over all group homomorphisms G → H, with no injectivity or surjectivity assumptions.
The notation βf should be understood as an endomorphism of H that may depend on f; no uniqueness is assumed.
The phrase 'inner automorphism of G' should be defined explicitly as conjugation by some element s ∈ G, i.e. g ↦ sgs^{-1}.
The phrase 'trivial endomorphism' should be defined explicitly as the constant homomorphism g ↦ 1_G.
If one uses the original Bergman formulation, the coherence condition must be stated explicitly: for every commuting triangle G --f--> H1 --h--> H2, one has βh∘f ∘ h = h ∘ βf.
refined_question: Let G be an arbitrary group and let α ∈ End(G). Assume that for every group H and every homomorphism f: G → H, there exists an endomorphism βf ∈ End(H) such that βf ∘ f = f ∘ α. Must it follow that either α is conjugation by some element s ∈ G (equivalently, α(g) = sgs^{-1} for all g ∈ G), or α is the trivial endomorphism g ↦ 1_G of G?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, in Bergman’s original formulation: if α ∈ End(G) is such that for every object f: G → H of the comma category (G↓Group) there exists βf ∈ End(H) with βf ∘ f = f ∘ α, must α be inner in the sense of Definition 4; that is, can the endomorphisms βf be chosen so that for every commuting triangle G --f--> H1 --h--> H2 one has βh∘f ∘ h = h ∘ βf, i.e. so that the family (βf) defines an endomorphism of the forgetful functor (G↓Group) → Group?
justification: In arXiv:1401.0300 the problem appears as Problem 21.14, already restated in the simplified form used in your draft: the conclusion is phrased directly as 'inner automorphism or trivial endomorphism.' Bergman’s original paper, however, formulates the question as a coherence problem for the family (βf) over the comma category (G↓Group). Theorem 1 identifies coherent systems of automorphisms with conjugation by a unique element of G, Theorem 2 packages this as automorphisms of the forgetful functor, Corollary 3 shows that allowing endomorphisms adds only the trivial case, and Definition 4/Question 5 package the open problem in exactly that language. So the sharp paper-faithful stand-alone question is your draft with the implicit definitions made explicit, while the only alternate formulation worth giving is the paper-explicit functorial one.
